title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1970-07-30

ai_review.summary: Good‑quality soundboard capture of a brief, folk‑filled acoustic set highlighted by “To Lay Me Down” and “Rosalie McFall,” though the bass is a bit over‑present.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clear soundboard source but suffers from an overly loud bass that makes the mix muddy in places. Musically the show shines as a short, relaxed acoustic set from July 30 1970, featuring standout performances of “To Lay Me Down,” “Rosalie McFall,” “I Hear a Voice Calling” and “Swing Low Sweet Chariot,” with warm vocals and gentle banter.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the acoustic performance and give 4‑5 stars, while a few note significant recording issues; the weighted average of the scores yields a solid mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear soundboard capture overall, but bass is often too loud causing muddiness; some high‑end harshness and occasional banter noise detract from guitar detail.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, folk‑centric acoustic set that feels relaxed and reverent; the sequence flows simply with gospel touches, though the limited length leaves listeners wishing for more.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s picking is praised, his vocal on “Swing Low” noted, and a brief curse at a heckler is mentioned.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as rich and warm by one reviewer.
